Division 10 encompasses formal and non-formal educational services, structured according to the International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED 2011). It covers the full spectrum of instruction from early childhood through to tertiary levels, as well as supplementary training and academic support services.

This division includes, among others:

*   **Formal Education Levels:** The provision of organized instructional programmes across early childhood and primary education (101), secondary education (102), post-secondary non-tertiary education (103), and tertiary education (104). These services lead to recognized certificates, diplomas, or degrees and encompass academic, vocational, and professional pathways, including those tailored for special educational needs.
*   **Education Not Defined by Level:** Supplementary and specialized instruction including independent private lessons, tutoring centers, homework assistance, and exam preparation (105). It also covers general and vocational adult training, language instruction, and technical or software training (105).
*   **Fees and Ancillary Costs:** All direct costs associated with education, including admission, registration, tuition, diploma, examination, graduation, and laboratory fees. It also includes costs for physical education and specific ancillary activities, such as excursions, field trips, or student exchanges, provided these are integral parts of the normal school programme. This encompasses delivery via radio, television, e-learning, and correspondence courses.

This does not include:
*   Childcare services that do not provide an educational programme (13.3.0.1).
*   Driving lessons (07.2.4.3).
*   Training courses for recreation and sports that are not part of a formal educational programme (09.4.6).
*   Education support services, such as health-care services (06).
*   Textbooks, academic journals, and removable media containing educational software (09.7.1.1).
*   Stationery (09.7.4.0).
*   School uniforms (03.1.2.4).
*   Catering services (11.1.2.1).
*   Accommodation services (11.2.0.3), unless the costs are explicitly integrated into a formal school programme as an excursion or student exchange.
*   Transport services, except in the case of excursions that are part of the normal school programme (07.3.2.3).

This category encompasses the initial stages of formal education, corresponding to levels 0 and 1 of the ISCED 2011 classification. It focuses on organized instructional programmes designed to foster the foundational cognitive, physical, social, and emotional development of children, as well as the acquisition of basic academic competencies.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Early Childhood Education (1010):** Organised educational programmes for children prior to the entry age of primary schooling, including centre-based, school-based, or hospital-based learning environments and specialised services for children with special educational needs.
*   **Primary Education (1010):** Core instructional programmes providing fundamental skills in reading, writing, and mathematics, including literacy or basic skills programmes for students who have surpassed the standard age for primary schooling, and education services for children with special educational needs.
*   **Supportive Educational Services (1010):** Ancillary costs such as excursions, travel, and accommodation that are directly integrated into the formal school curriculum.

This does not include childcare services that do not provide an educational programme (13.3.0.1).

This category includes, among others:

*   **Early Childhood Education (10101):** Organised instruction for children prior to the entry age of primary education, including centre-based, school-based, or hospital-based learning environments, as well as specialised services for children with special educational needs.
*   **Primary Education (10102):** Core instructional programmes that provide fundamental skills in reading, writing, and mathematics, including literacy or basic skills programmes for students who have surpassed the standard age for primary schooling, and organised instruction for children with special needs.
*   **Supportive Educational Services (10101, 10102):** Excursions and related travel or accommodation costs that are integrated into the formal school curriculum.

This does not include childcare services that do not provide an educational programme (13.3.0.1).

It is designed to provide the foundational skills and knowledge necessary for further studies at post-secondary or tertiary levels, entry into the labour market, or both.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Educational Programmes:** Academic and subject-oriented secondary education, as well as specialized study options including vocational education and training (Secondary education (S)).
*   **Targeted and Alternative Provision:** Secondary education programmes tailored for adults and young people, including second-chance or reintegration programmes, as well as out-of-school secondary education initiatives (Secondary education (S)).
*   **Specialized Support:** Education services specifically designed for adolescents with special educational needs (Secondary education (S)).
*   **Associated Educational Activities:** Costs related to excursions or student exchanges that constitute an integral part of the standard school curriculum, including associated travel and accommodation expenses (Secondary education (S)).

This category encompasses post-secondary non-tertiary education, which provides learning experiences that build upon upper secondary education without reaching the complexity of tertiary-level studies. It is primarily designed to facilitate direct entry into the labour market or to provide the necessary qualifications for individuals to progress to tertiary education.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Vocational and Specialization Programmes:** Learning pathways for those who have completed upper secondary education but require further qualifications for specific employment or wish to specialize in a particular field (Post-secondary non-tertiary education (S)).
*   **Preparatory and General Programmes:** Programmes designed to bridge the gap for students who lack the specific qualifications required for tertiary education (Post-secondary non-tertiary education (S)).
*   **Alternative and Specialized Educational Services:** Out-of-school post-secondary education for young people and adults, as well as dedicated education services for individuals with special educational needs (Post-secondary non-tertiary education (S)).
*   **Educational Ancillary Activities:** Costs related to excursions or student exchanges, including travel and accommodation, provided they are an integral part of the normal school programme (Post-secondary non-tertiary education (S)).

This category does not include any specific exclusions.

This category encompasses tertiary education programmes that build upon secondary education, providing learning activities within specialized fields at a high level of complexity and specialization. It covers the full spectrum of post-secondary instruction, ranging from advanced vocational and professional training to comprehensive academic and doctoral research programmes.

This category includes levels 5, 6, 7, and 8 of the ISCED 2011 classification (Tertiary education). This includes, among others:

*   **Academic and Professional Programmes:** Formal higher education pathways leading to recognized academic degrees or professional certifications, as well as advanced research programmes that result in qualifications based on original research and advanced study (Tertiary education - 1040).
*   **Supportive Educational Activities:** Costs related to excursions or student exchanges that are integral to the normal school programme, including travel and accommodation, as well as university admission testing fees (Tertiary education - 1040).

This category encompasses educational and instructional activities that are not structured according to specific formal education levels. It covers a broad range of supplementary academic support and specialized short-term training programs designed for both children and adults.

The scope of this category is organized into the following areas:

*   **Tutoring and Academic Support:** This includes services designed to assist students with formal education requirements, such as independent private lessons, tutoring centers, homework assistance, online tutoring services, and specialized exam preparation courses (1050).
*   **General and Vocational Training:** This includes short educational courses for adults that do not require prior specific instruction, such as cultural development programs and various types of vocational training (1050).
*   **Language and Technical Instruction:** This includes language proficiency testing, language courses provided in classroom or online settings, language immersion courses, international travel for language learning purposes, and instructional courses for computer usage or specific software applications (1050).

This category does not include driving lessons (07.2.4.3), training courses for recreation and sports that are not part of a formal educational programme (09.4.6), or removable media containing foreign language learning software (09.7.1.1).

Division 11 encompasses services related to the commercial provision of prepared food and beverages for immediate consumption, as well as temporary accommodation services for visitors and travellers away from their principal or secondary residence. This category covers both professional hospitality establishments and institutional settings where these services are provided and separately invoiced.

This includes, among others:

*   **Food and Beverage Serving Services:** The preparation and provision of meals and drinks through commercial hospitality outlets, including full-service restaurants, cafés, fast-food establishments, refreshment stands, and specialized venues like ice-cream parlours and automat restaurants (111). It also covers institutional catering services within schools, universities, workplaces, and healthcare facilities (111).
*   **Accommodation Services:** The provision of lodging for travellers in a wide variety of facilities, such as hotels, motels, inns, pensions, bed and breakfasts, resorts, and holiday villages (112). This cluster also includes recreational accommodation like camping sites, mountain refuges, and youth hostels, as well as institutional living quarters such as student dormitories (when separately priced) and worker accommodation (112). Ancillary costs associated with these stays, such as service fees for porters, housekeeping, and platform booking fees, are also included (112).

This does not include:
*   Accommodation used as a permanent principal or secondary residence (division 04).
*   Food and beverage items purchased from supermarkets, markets, or vending machines (not connected to a restaurant).
*   Standalone tobacco purchases.
*   Food and beverage services provided on public transport, within package holidays, or integrated into entrance fees for recreational, cultural, or sporting venues.
*   Non-medical retirement homes or residences for disabled or maladjusted persons (13.3).
*   Telephone calls and other utility services not integrated into the accommodation price.

details.excludes: * permanent principal or secondary residence accommodation (division 4)

This category encompasses food and beverage serving services provided to consumers across various hospitality, institutional, and professional settings. It covers the preparation and provision of meals and drinks intended for immediate consumption, whether provided through commercial hospitality establishments or specialized catering facilities.

This includes, among others:

*   **Commercial Hospitality Services:** Services provided by restaurants, cafés, and similar facilities offering full, limited, or self-service options, including hotels (when priced separately), recreational, cultural, or sporting venues (1111). It also encompasses gratuities and tips provided for these services (11111, 11112).

This does not include:

This category encompasses accommodation services provided to visitors and travellers away from their permanent principal or secondary residence. It covers a diverse range of professional lodging facilities, institutional living quarters, and associated service fees.

This includes, among others:

*   **Commercial and Short-term Lodging:** Professional hospitality services including resorts, hotels (including those letting rooms by the hour), motels, inns, pensions, guesthouses, "bed and breakfast" establishments, and timeshare units (1120).
*   **Recreational and Outdoor Accommodation:** Lodging for holidaymakers and outdoor enthusiasts, such as holiday villages, holiday centres, bungalows, chalets, housekeeping cottages, cabins, camping sites, onsite non-mobile caravans and boats, youth hostels, and mountain refuges (1120).
*   **Institutional and Worker Accommodation:** Provision of living quarters within educational settings, such as student residences and dormitories for schools and universities (when the service is separately priced), as well as hostels and other accommodations specifically for workers (1120).
*   **Ancillary and Intermediary Services:** Related costs such as railway sleeping cars (when separately priced), website fees for listing or renting lodging, travel agency fees for accommodation (if priced separately), and tips or gratuities for bellmen, porters, and housekeeping staff (1120).

This does not include: payments by households for rooms occupied as a main residence (04.1.1.0) or as a secondary residence (04.1.2.1); telephone calls (08.3.1.0); package holidays (09.8.0.0); breakfast, meals, and other food and beverages provided in accommodation if separately priced (11.1.1); or non-medical retirement homes and residences for disabled or maladjusted persons (13.3.0.2).

Division 12 encompasses a broad spectrum of services provided by financial corporations, covering both insurance products and various financial intermediation activities. These services are characterized by a combination of explicit service fees and implicit charges, the latter of which are often embedded within interest rate spreads or the administrative costs of risk-pooling and asset management.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Insurance Services (121):** This cluster covers the service charges (administrative and operational costs) associated with personal risk protection. It includes life and accident insurance (1211), health-related and medical coverage (1212), dwelling insurance for tenants and owner-occupiers (1213), transport-related insurance including personal vehicles and travel (1214), and other specialized personal policies such as civil liability, legal expenses, and pet insurance (1219).
*   **Financial Services (122):** This cluster covers the costs of financial intermediation and auxiliary financial activities. It includes Financial Intermediation Services Indirectly Measured (FISIM) derived from interest rate spreads on loans and deposits (1221), explicit banking and transaction fees levied by deposit-taking institutions (1222), and specialized financial services such as investment management, pension fund administration, currency exchange, and financial brokerage and consultancy (1229).

This does not include service charges paid by owner-occupiers for insurance policies that are considered intermediate consumption of landlords, specific remittance fees when classified under alternative frameworks, or financial services explicitly categorized under other insurance or specialized financial frameworks.

It reflects the administrative and operational costs (service charges) embedded in these insurance premiums, as measured by the difference between premiums earned (plus investment income) and adjusted claims or benefits due.

This includes, among others:
*   **Life and Accident Protection:** Service charges for life insurance, annuities, death benefit insurance, education insurance, funeral insurance, and accident insurance (1211).
*   **Health-related Insurance:** Service charges for direct sickness insurance, social and supplementary health insurance, disability and critical illness coverage, long-term care, prescription drug coverage, and travel health or medical transport insurance (1212).

*   **Transport Insurance:** Service charges for insurance related to personal transport equipment (cars, motorcycles, bicycles, boats, yachts, sailboats, and airplanes), including civil liability, as well as travel insurance covering trip cancellations and luggage protection (1214).
*   **Other Personal Insurance:** Service charges for general civil liability insurance, legal expense insurance, standardized guarantees, and pet medical insurance (1219).

This does not include:
*   Service charges paid by owner-occupiers for insurance policies typically taken out by landlords, which are considered intermediate consumption (1213).
*   Travel health insurance (1212).

This category encompasses a comprehensive range of financial services, categorized by both financial intermediation services indirectly measured (FISIM) and explicit service fees or charges levied by financial institutions and intermediaries. It covers the costs associated with banking, investment management, pension administration, and the facilitation of financial transactions and remittances.

This includes, among others:

*   **Financial Intermediation Services Indirectly Measured (FISIM):** This covers the implicit charges embedded in interest rate spreads provided by deposit-taking corporations, moneylenders, credit card issuers, retail finance associates, pawnshops, and entities involved in specialized lending such as student and import/export loans (1221).
*   **Explicit Banking Charges:** This includes actual fees and service charges levied by deposit-taking institutions, such as commercial banks, credit unions, cooperative banks, savings banks, and postal savings banks (1222).
*   **Auxiliary and Specialized Financial Services:** This covers actual and implicit charges for services provided by money changers, remittance agents, money market and non-money market investment funds, financial brokers, and consultants. It also encompasses the administrative and implicit charges of pension funds and other miscellaneous financial services (1229).

This does not include remittance fees associated with the transfer of funds when specifically classified elsewhere (1222), or financial services explicitly categorized under other insurance or specialized financial frameworks.

This category encompasses the financial intermediation services indirectly measured (FISIM) provided by various financial institutions, representing the implicit charges for services that are embedded within interest rate spreads rather than explicitly billed. It is calculated as the total difference between the actual interest receivable by financial corporations and the reference rate of interest on loans, added to the difference between the reference rate and the actual interest payable by these corporations on customer deposits.

This category includes, among others, the financial intermediation services indirectly measured (FISIM) of deposit-taking corporations (12210). Furthermore, it includes implicit financial services provided by various other lending entities, such as moneylenders, credit card issuers, and the finance associates of retailers responsible for providing loans (12210). This also encompasses the services of pawnshops and specialized corporations involved in lending activities, including the provision of student loans and import/export financing (12210).

This category does not include explicit financial service fees or commissions that are charged separately from interest rate margins.

detailled_description:
Division 13 encompasses a wide range of goods and services related to individual grooming, personal effects, social care, and various administrative or specialized personal services. It serves to aggregate items and activities essential for daily living that are not categorized within more specific domains such as health, housing, or recreation.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Personal Care:** Goods and services for hygiene, grooming, and aesthetic maintenance, including electric and non-electric appliances (e.g., razors, hairdryers, toothbrushes), cosmetic products (perfumes, make-up), and professional services such as hairdressing, barbering, manicures, and body treatments (131).
*   **Personal Effects:** A diverse array of goods for personal adornment, ritual, and transit. This includes jewellery and timepieces, religious and devotional articles, infant care items (diapers, strollers), smoking accessories, travel goods (suitcases, handbags), and miscellaneous articles such as umbrellas, sunglasses, and funerary goods (132).
*   **Social Protection:** Non-medical support services focused on the welfare and integration of vulnerable individuals. This includes formal childcare facilities (nurseries, day-care centers), non-medical residential care for the elderly or disabled, and community-based support services like home-care assistance and family counseling (133).
*   **Miscellaneous Services:** A broad spectrum of professional and social services, including legal, notary, and accounting fees, real estate and auctioneering services, funeral and burial services, and religious ceremonies. It also covers specialized personal services such as those provided by private detectives, dating agencies, bodyguards, and administrative document processing fees (139).

This does not include household clocks and ornaments (05), items primarily serving as a store of value (e.g., bullion), educational kindergartens (10), fitness centres (09), or medical-integrated services such as nursing homes and medical spas (06). Additionally, it excludes specific textiles like fabric handkerchiefs (03), individual babysitting (05), and food or beverages purchased within establishments classified as personal services (11).

*   **Hairdressing and personal grooming services:** Professional services including hairdressing and barbering for all ages, as well as aesthetic body treatments such as manicures, pedicures, depilation, tanning, saunas, Turkish baths, non-medical massages, diet clubs, and tattooing or piercing services (1313).

This category encompasses a diverse range of personal items, equipment for daily use, and specialized articles, as well as the associated services for their repair and hire. It is designed to capture miscellaneous personal goods not classified elsewhere, including items for transit, infant care, and lifestyle needs.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Travel and Personal Carriers:** A wide variety of goods for transporting personal effects, such as suitcases, trunks, travel bags, attaché cases, satchels, handbags, wallets, purses, and backpacks intended for school or general travel (13291).
*   **Articles for Babies:** Essential items for infant care, including diapers (nappies) of any material, baby carriages, pushchairs/strollers, carrycots, recliners, back carriers, front carriers, and harnesses for babies (13291).
*   **Articles for Smokers:** Tobacco-related accessories such as pipes, lighters (including lighter fuel), cigarette cases, cigar cutters, ashtrays, and electronic cigarette devices (13291).

*   **Funerary Articles:** Specialized items required for burial and commemoration, including coffins, gravestones, urns, and burial shrouds (13291).
*   **Services:** The repair and hire of the personal effects listed above, where the cost of materials is included only if they are not separately priced (13292).

This does not include garden or beach umbrellas and parasols (05.1.1.2; 09.2.2.2), baby furniture (05.1.1.1), shopping bags (05.2.1.9), feeding bottles (05.4.0.3), baby scales (06.1.2.1), car seats for babies (07.2.1.3), protective glasses specifically for sports (09.2.2.1), or backpacks intended for camping and open-air recreation (09.2.2.2).

Social protection encompasses non-medical support and care services designed to promote the welfare, independence, and social integration of vulnerable individuals and families. This category focuses on providing custodial and community-based assistance rather than integrated medical treatment.

This includes, among others:

*   **Childcare Services:** Facilities providing non-educational child-minding and care, such as nurseries, crèches, day-care centers, after-school facilities, wet nurses, play schools, and kindergartens (1330).
*   **Support for the Elderly and Disabled:** Non-medical residential care, including retirement homes and residences for disabled or maladjusted persons (1330). It also covers community-based support services aimed at maintaining independence, such as home-cleaning services, meal programs, and non-medical day-care or holiday-care services (1330).
*   **Family and Specialized Support:** Institutional support for persons with disabilities where the primary objective is to overcome specific impairments, as well as broader social services such as family counseling, guidance, arbitration, fostering, and adoption services (1330).

This does not include individual babysitting services (05.6.2.1) or educational kindergartens (10.1.0.1). Furthermore, it excludes social care services integrated into a medical package, such as nursing homes, convalescent hospitals, hospices, palliative care, or facilities for mental health, substance abuse, or alcoholism, which are classified under medical or health service categories (06.2.3 and 06.3.2).

This category encompasses social protection services designed to provide non-medical support and care for children, the elderly, individuals with disabilities, and families in need. It includes residential, day-care, and community-based support services aimed at facilitating daily living, integration, and social welfare.

The scope of this category includes:

*   **Childcare Services:** Facilities providing child-minding outside the home, such as nurseries, crèches, day-care facilities, after-school centers, wet nurses, play schools, and kindergartens, provided that the primary function is custodial rather than educational (13301).
*   **Residential and Support Services for Elderly and Disabled Persons:** Non-medical residential care for the elderly and disabled, including retirement homes and residences for disabled or maladjusted persons (13302). It also covers home-based assistance to help these individuals maintain independence, including meal programs, home-cleaning services, and non-medical day-care or holiday-care services (13303).
*   **Specialized Social and Family Support:** Educational institutions for persons with disabilities where the core objective is to assist students in overcoming their specific disabilities, as well as broader social services such as family counselling, guidance, arbitration, fostering, and adoption services (13309).

This category does not include services where social care is integrated into a medical package, such as nursing homes, convalescent hospitals, hospices, palliative care, or facilities for mental health, substance abuse, or alcoholism (where medical services are provided). Additionally, it excludes individual babysitting services (05.6.2.1), educational kindergartens (10.1.0.1), and services of mental health convalescent homes or hospitals (06.3.2.0).

This category encompasses a broad range of miscellaneous personal, professional, administrative, and social services that do not fall under other specific functional classifications. It covers essential legal and financial support, specialized personal assistance, funeral and religious requirements, and various community-based administrative and social events.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Professional and Administrative Services:** Fees for legal and financial services, including those provided by lawyers, notaries, and accountants; services provided by employment agencies; fees for the issuance of administrative documents, such as birth, marriage, and death certificates; costs for document reproduction and photocopying; and fees for licenses, such as firearm licences (1390).
*   **Estate and Intermediary Services:** Services related to the management and sale of assets, including housing and estate agents, auctioneers, and salesroom operators (1390).
*   **Funeral and Religious Services:** Expenses for funeral services and the work of undertakers, as well as expenditures associated with religious ceremonies, such as baptisms, requiems, and weddings (1390).
*   **Social and Personal Services:** Services provided by sex workers and prostitutes; specialized personal services including dating and matrimonial agencies, marriage guidance counseling, private detectives, bodyguards, and the services of astrologers, palmists, and graphologists (1390).
*   **Miscellaneous Services and Fees:** Expenditures for non-religious social events, such as debutante balls or "quinceañera" celebrations; public writing and advertising services, including newspaper notices; and miscellaneous concessions for facilities such as toilets, cloakrooms, or seats (1390).

This does not include food or beverages consumed in brothels if they are priced separately (11.1.1).

This category encompasses the individual consumption expenditure of Non-profit Institutions Serving Households (NPISHs), representing the value of goods and services provided by these institutions to households either for free or at prices that are not economically significant. It provides a comprehensive framework for classifying the functional purposes of NPISH activities, aligning with international statistical standards including the Classification of the Purposes of Non-Profit Institutions Serving Households (COPNI) and relevant COICOP divisions.

This category includes the following functional clusters:

*   **Housing:** Expenditure related to the provision and occupation of residential housing, covering both actual and imputed rentals (Housing / 141).
*   **Health:** A wide range of medical and health-related services, including pharmaceutical products, therapeutic appliances, outpatient consultations (medical, dental, and paramedical), and hospital and other health services (Health / 142).
*   **Recreation and Culture:** Services that facilitate public engagement in leisure and cultural life, including recreational and sporting infrastructure, as well as access to museums, libraries, and performing arts (Recreation and culture / 143).
*   **Education:** The provision of formal and non-formal educational services across all stages, from early childhood and primary schooling through to tertiary and specialized educational support (Education / 144).
*   **Social Protection:** Interventions and support mechanisms designed to assist individuals and families in managing social risks and vulnerabilities (Social protection / 145).
*   **Other Services:** Miscellaneous services provided by NPISHs not covered elsewhere, including religious and ideological activities, organizational and representational services (such as labour unions and political parties), and environmental protection initiatives (Other services / 146).

This category does not include services or equipment classified outside the scope of NPISH consumption, such as activities provided directly by government entities or commercial providers. It also excludes services explicitly governed by other functional classifications that fall outside the defined scope of NPISH service provision, including certain professional, administrative, or operational costs that do not meet the criteria for individual consumption expenditure.

This category encompasses expenditure related to the provision and occupation of residential housing, serving as a consolidated reporting framework for both rented and owner-occupied dwellings. It bridges international standards for individual consumption and non-profit institutional reporting, aligning with COICOP groups 04.1 and 15.1, as well as COPNI group 01.0.

This category includes the following housing services:
*   **Rental Expenditures:** This covers actual rentals paid by tenants for residential accommodation (Housing (S) / 1410).
*   **Imputed Rentals:** This covers the imputed rentals for owner-occupied dwellings, representing the cost of housing services derived from homeownership (Housing (S) / 1410).

This category encompasses expenditure related to housing, specifically covering services that provide residential accommodation. It aligns with the functional definitions used in established international statistical classifications, bridging the reporting frameworks for non-profit institutions and individual consumption.

This category includes the actual and imputed rentals for housing as defined under COICOP classes 04.1.1 (Actual rentals paid by tenants) and 15.1.0 (Imputed rentals of owner-occupied dwellings). The functional scope of this class is identical to that covered under COPNI class 01.0.0.
The same function is covered under COPNI class 01.0.0. This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 04.1.1 and 15.1.0.

This category encompasses a comprehensive range of health-related goods and services, including medical products, therapeutic equipment, outpatient care, and hospital services, aimed at the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of human health conditions. It aligns with the functional classifications defined under COICOP division 06 and group 15.2, as well as COPNI groups 02.1 to 02.6.

This category includes, among others:

*   **Medical and Pharmaceutical Products:** This includes medicinal preparations, drugs, and pharmaceutical items intended for human health (1421), as well as various non-durable medical supplies and miscellaneous medical products (1422). It also covers therapeutic appliances, medical devices, and technical aids designed for the management or alleviation of physical impairments (1423).
*   **Outpatient Medical and Paramedical Services:** This includes consultations and treatments provided by medical, dental, and paramedical practitioners that do not require an overnight hospital stay. This encompasses general outpatient medical services (1424), specialized dental treatments provided by dentists, oral surgeons, and orthodontists (1425), and other paramedical support, diagnostic, and therapeutic interventions (1426).
*   **Hospital and Other Health Services:** This includes all inpatient and outpatient care administered within a hospital setting (1427), as well as residual health-related services aimed at the protection, promotion, and restoration of public and individual health (1428).

This category does not include services or equipment classified outside the scope of personal health consumption or those specifically governed by non-health related functional classifications.

This category encompasses the provision, administration, and support of formal and non-formal educational services across all stages of learning. This includes, among others:
*   **Foundational and Secondary Education:** The provision of early childhood and primary education (Pre-primary and primary education, 1441) and secondary-level schooling (Secondary education, 1442).
*   **Advanced and Transitional Education:** Programs that facilitate the transition between secondary and tertiary levels (Post-secondary non-tertiary education, 1443) and tertiary-level academic or professional qualifications provided by universities and higher education institutions (Tertiary education, 1444).

This does not include social protection services provided directly by government entities or commercial providers outside the scope of non-profit institutions serving households.

This category covers social protection services provided by non-profit institutions serving households. It encompasses activities and support mechanisms designed to assist individuals and families in managing various social risks, aligned with international statistical standards for the classification of individual consumption by purpose (COICOP) and the classification of the purposes of non-profit institutions serving households (COPNI).

This category includes social protection functions corresponding to COPNI classes 05.1.0 (Social protection) and 05.2.0 (Other social services), as well as COICOP classes 13.3.0 (Social protection services) and 15.5.0 (Individual social protection services).
The same function is covered under COPNI classes 05.1.0 and 05.2.0. This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 13.3.0 and 15.5.0.

This category encompasses a wide range of services provided by non-profit institutions serving households (NPISHs) that are not classified under other specific functional headings. It primarily covers collective services related to religious, political, social, environmental, and other miscellaneous activities.

This includes, among others:
*   **Religious and ideological services:** Expenditures associated with the practice of religion, including contributions and membership fees to religious organizations (1461).
*   **Organizational and representational services:** Activities carried out by political parties, labour unions, and professional organizations aimed at advocating for the interests of their members or the public (1462).
*   **Environmental protection:** Initiatives and services dedicated to the prevention or reduction of pollution and the preservation of natural resources (1463).
*   **Miscellaneous services:** Various services not elsewhere classified that fall under general service categories (1464).

These functions are primarily aligned with the COPNI (Classification of the Purposes of Non-Profit Institutions Serving Households) divisions 06.0, 07.1, 07.2, 07.3, 08.1, 08.2, 09.1, and 09.2.

This category does not include the administrative or operational costs of religious institutions when classified elsewhere as non-profit institutions under different functional headings, nor does it include charitable donations for purposes other than religious service provision if those activities are classified under other functional categories. Additionally, it generally does not encompass services explicitly covered within the standard COICOP divisions 01 to 13 or division 15, with the sole exception of the specific religious services noted above.

This category encompasses services related to religious organizations and institutions, focusing on expenditures associated with the practice of religion. It captures the financial interactions of households with religious bodies, reflecting the economic dimension of religious participation.

This category includes contributions, membership fees, and payments for services or activities provided by religious organizations (Religion (S)).

This category does not include the administrative or operational costs of religious institutions when classified as non-profit institutions serving households under different functional headings, nor does it include charitable donations for purposes other than religious service provision if classified elsewhere.
The same function is covered under COPNI class 06.0.0. This subclass corresponds to COICOP subclass 13.9.0.2.

description: Political parties, labour and professional organizations (S)
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the services and activities provided by organizations serving the interests of specific groups, including political parties, trade unions, and professional associations. It primarily reflects the functional expenditure associated with institutions that advocate for the political, economic, and social interests of their members or the public.

This includes the administrative, operational, and representational activities of political parties, labour unions, and professional organizations (14620). Note that this category corresponds to the functional classifications defined under COPNI classes 07.1.0, 07.2.0, and 07.3.0.

description: Political parties, labour and professional organizations (S)
detailled_description: The same function is covered under COPNI classes 07.1.0, 07.2.0 and 07.3.0.

This category encompasses activities and services dedicated to the protection of the environment, including the prevention, reduction, or elimination of pollution and other forms of environmental degradation. It covers initiatives aimed at preserving the quality of natural resources and maintaining ecological balance through systematic environmental management.

This category aligns with the functional scope defined under the Classification of the Purposes of Non-Profit Institutions Serving Households (COPNI), specifically addressing the functions categorized under classes 08.1.0 and 08.2.0.
The same function is covered under COPNI classes 08.1.0 and 08.2.0.

This category encompasses miscellaneous services that are not elsewhere classified (n.e.c.) and do not fall under other specific service categories. This classification aligns with the functional scope covered under COPNI classes 09.1.0 (Services n.e.c.) and 09.2.0 (Services n.e.c.).
The same function is covered under COPNI classes 09.1.0 and 09.2.0.

description: Individual consumption expenditure of general government
detailled_description:
This category encompasses the individual consumption expenditure of general government, covering the provision of goods and services that are financed by government units and provided to individual households. It covers a broad spectrum of essential social and personal services, including housing support, healthcare, recreational and cultural activities, formal education, and social protection mechanisms.

This includes, among others:

*   **Housing:** Expenditure related to the provision of housing services, including costs for actual and imputed rentals (151).
*   **Health:** A comprehensive range of medical products, therapeutic equipment, and diverse professional healthcare services provided in outpatient, hospital, and public health settings (152).
*   **Recreation and Culture:** The provision, administration, and operational support of services, facilities, and events dedicated to leisure, physical activity, and cultural expression (153).
*   **Education:** The provision and support of formal educational services across all levels—from early childhood and primary schooling (1541) through secondary (1542) to post-secondary and tertiary education (1543, 1544)—as well as undefined educational programs (1545) and ancillary educational services (1546).
*   **Social Protection:** Interventions designed to support individuals against the risks of social exclusion, poverty, and vulnerability, including sickness and disability support, old-age pensions, family benefits, and unemployment assistance (155).

This category does not include services classified under distinct functional headings outside the scope of individual consumption, such as research and development in social protection (COFOG 10.6.0), non-formal vocational training programs that do not form part of the classified educational system, or retail-based commercial entertainment and health products that fall outside the defined public provision frameworks.

This category encompasses expenditure related to the provision of housing services, specifically covering the costs associated with both actual and imputed rentals for housing. It functions as a consolidated classification for housing-related outlays, aligning with international reporting standards, notably corresponding to COFOG group 10.6 and COICOP groups 04.1 and 14.1 (1510 Housing (S)).

This category encompasses expenditure related to the provision of housing services, including the costs associated with actual and imputed rentals for housing. It serves as a consolidated classification that aligns with international reporting standards, specifically corresponding to COFOG class 10.6.0 and COICOP classes 04.1.1 and 14.1.0.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 10.6.0.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 04.1.1 and 14.1.0.

The Health category encompasses a comprehensive range of medical products, therapeutic equipment, and diverse healthcare services designed to maintain, restore, or improve individual and community health. This category covers both goods consumed for personal health and professional services provided in outpatient, hospital, and public health settings, aligning with COFOG groups 07.1 to 07.4 and COICOP division 06 and group 14.2.

This category includes, among others:
*   **Medical Goods:** Pharmaceutical products and medicinal preparations (1521), miscellaneous non-durable medical products (1522), and therapeutic appliances and equipment, including prosthetic and orthopedic devices (1523).
*   **Outpatient Services:** General medical services, including consultations and diagnostic procedures (1524), dental services provided by specialists (1525), and paramedical support services provided outside of hospital settings (1526).
*   **Institutional and Community Services:** Inpatient and hospital-based diagnostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitative care (1527), as well as public health services focused on the monitoring and promotion of health for community or population groups (1528).

This does not include inpatient hospital services or primary clinical services provided by physicians when classified under specific paramedical categories (1526). Furthermore, it excludes medical products or equipment that are explicitly categorized within the pharmaceutical or therapeutic appliance classes (1522, 1523).

This category encompasses all pharmaceutical products designed for medical use, including medicinal preparations and substances. It specifically covers non-durable goods intended for the treatment, prevention, or management of health conditions, corresponding to the medical products defined under international standard classifications. This class is functionally equivalent to COFOG class 07.1.1 and corresponds to COICOP classes 06.1.1 and 14.2.1.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 07.1.1.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 06.1.1 and 14.2.1.

This category covers the provision and consumption of miscellaneous medical products that are not classified under other specific medical goods categories. It functions as a residual grouping for essential health-related items, ensuring comprehensive coverage of non-durable medical goods within the framework of personal health expenditure.

This category includes medical products and items defined under the corresponding classifications for non-durable medical goods (subclass 15220). The scope of this category is consistent with the classification standards for health-related expenditures, specifically aligning with COFOG class 07.1.2 (Other medical products) and COICOP classes 06.1.2 and 14.2.2.

This category does not include pharmaceutical products, therapeutic appliances, or medical equipment that are explicitly classified under other specific medical product codes.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 07.1.2.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 06.1.2 and 14.2.2.

This category encompasses therapeutic appliances and equipment intended for the alleviation, treatment, or compensation of physical disabilities, injuries, or health conditions. It covers a range of specialized medical devices designed to support bodily functions or assist in the rehabilitation and daily living of individuals with specific medical requirements.

This category corresponds to COICOP classes 06.1.3 and 14.2.3, and its function is aligned with COFOG class 07.1.3. It includes various types of medical apparatus, technical aids, and prosthetic or orthopedic devices necessary for therapeutic interventions.

This category does not include general medical supplies or diagnostic equipment classified under other specific medical and health categories.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 07.1.3.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 06.1.3 and 14.2.3.

This category encompasses outpatient medical services provided by healthcare professionals, covering consultations, diagnostic procedures, and therapeutic treatments that do not require an overnight hospital stay. It corresponds to the functions identified in COFOG classes 07.2.1 and 07.2.2, as well as the consumption classifications defined in COICOP classes 06.2.1, 06.2.3, and 14.2.4.
The same function is covered under COFOG classes 07.2.1 and 07.2.2.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 06.2.1, 06.2.3 and 14.2.4.

This category encompasses outpatient dental services provided to individuals by dentists, oral surgeons, or other dental specialists. It covers the full spectrum of non-hospitalized dental care, including routine check-ups, diagnostic procedures, preventative treatments, and surgical interventions. This class corresponds to COICOP classes 06.2.2 and 14.2.5, and the same functional scope is covered under COFOG class 07.2.3.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 07.2.3.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 06.2.2 and 14.2.5.

This category encompasses outpatient paramedical services provided to individuals, covering a range of professional health support functions performed outside of hospital inpatient settings. It aligns with the functional classification of healthcare services that support primary medical treatment, rehabilitation, and specialized non-physician health care.

This category includes, among others, the provision of specialized paramedical services (15260). These services correspond to the activities categorized under COICOP classes 06.1.4, 06.2.1, 06.2.3, 06.4, and 14.2.6, and are functionally aligned with COFOG class 07.2.4.

This category does not include inpatient hospital services or medical services provided directly by general practitioners or specialized medical doctors in their primary clinical capacity.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 07.2.4.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 06.1.4, 06.2.1, 06.2.3, 06.4 and 14.2.6.

This category encompasses all inpatient and hospital-based medical services provided to patients. It covers the full range of diagnostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitative care delivered within hospital settings, consistent with the classifications defined under COFOG classes 07.3.1, 07.3.2, 07.3.3, and 07.3.4, and corresponds to COICOP group 06.3 and class 14.2.7.
The same function is covered under COFOG classes 07.3.1, 07.3.2, 07.3.3 and 07.3.4.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP group 06.3 and class 14.2.7.

This category encompasses the provision of public health services directed at the community or specific population groups rather than individual patients. It includes functions and activities dedicated to the monitoring, protection, and promotion of public health, corresponding to the classifications defined under COFOG class 07.4.0.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 07.4.0.

The category "Recreation and culture" encompasses the provision, administration, and operational support of services, facilities, and events dedicated to leisure, physical activity, and cultural expression. It covers the institutional and organizational frameworks that facilitate participation in sporting, recreational, and artistic activities.

This category includes, among others:
*   **Recreational and sporting services (1531):** The provision and management of infrastructure for physical exercise, leisure, and competitive sports, including the organizational support for recreational clubs and sporting events.
*   **Cultural services (1532):** The management and promotion of institutions and events dedicated to arts, heritage, and cultural expression, including the operational support for cultural functions.

This group corresponds to the COFOG groups 08.1 (Recreational and sporting services) and 08.2 (Cultural services), as well as the COICOP divisions 09.4, 09.6, and 14.3.

This category does not include services that are classified under distinct educational or social protection functional headings, nor does it encompass the retail sale of sporting or recreational equipment, or the operation of facilities primarily intended for commercial entertainment that fall outside the defined scope of public or recreational sporting and cultural services.

This category encompasses services provided for recreational and sporting activities, focusing on the provision of facilities and organizational support for leisure, physical exercise, and competitive sports. It covers the operational functions associated with public and private recreational infrastructure and sporting events.

This class includes all recreational and sporting services as defined within the functional classification frameworks. It corresponds to COFOG class 08.1.0, which pertains to the administration, support, and operation of facilities for recreational, cultural, and sporting activities, as well as the provision of COICOP group 09.4 (Recreational and cultural services) and class 14.3.1 (Services of sport and recreation clubs).

This category does not include services that fall under distinct cultural, educational, or social protection functional classifications, nor does it encompass the retail sale of sporting equipment or the operation of facilities primarily intended for commercial entertainment or non-sporting social gatherings.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 08.1.0.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP group 09.4 and class 14.3.1.

This category encompasses services related to cultural activities, facilities, and the promotion of arts and heritage. It covers the provision and management of institutions and events dedicated to cultural expression and preservation.

This includes, among others, the operational services and support for cultural functions (15320). 

This category does not include other specific recreational or sporting services, which are classified under separate functional headings.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 08.2.0.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP group 09.6 and class 14.3.2.

This category encompasses the provision, administration, and support of formal educational services across all stages of instruction, as well as ancillary services that facilitate the functioning of the education system. It covers the full spectrum of academic and professional development, ranging from foundational early childhood and primary schooling through to advanced tertiary education and specialized programs that cannot be defined by a specific educational level.

This includes, among others:
*   **Early Childhood and Foundational Education:** Programs provided at the pre-primary level and the initial years of compulsory primary instruction (Pre-primary and primary education 1541).
*   **Secondary Education:** Formal educational programs at the lower and upper secondary levels designed to prepare students for tertiary studies or entry into the labor market (Secondary education 1542).
*   **Post-Secondary and Tertiary Education:** Programs bridging the gap between secondary and higher education that do not lead to a formal tertiary degree (Post-secondary non-tertiary education 1543), as well as advanced post-secondary programs leading to recognized academic or professional qualifications (Tertiary education 1544).
*   **Supplementary and Support Services:** Educational programs that are not definable by a specific level of schooling (Education not defined by level 1545) and ancillary services necessary to support the delivery of educational activities (Subsidiary services to education 1546).

This category does not include programs that fall outside the definitions of formal educational levels as specified in international standards (COFOG 09.1–09.6 and COICOP division 10/group 14.4), nor does it include non-formal vocational training programs that do not form part of the classified educational system.

This category encompasses educational services provided at the pre-primary and primary levels, covering the foundational stages of formal schooling. It focuses on the provision of early childhood education and the initial years of compulsory primary instruction, aligning with established international statistical classifications for education functions and individual consumption.

This category includes expenditure and services related to pre-primary education, which precedes the compulsory primary stage, and primary education, which marks the commencement of the formal school system (Pre-primary and primary education 15410).

This category does not include secondary or tertiary education, specialized non-formal training programs, or other educational levels not explicitly classified under pre-primary or primary schooling.
The same function is covered under COFOG classes 09.1.1 and 09.1.2.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 10.1.0 and 14.4.1.

This category encompasses secondary education, covering both lower secondary and upper secondary levels of schooling. It provides for the provision of educational programs designed to complete the basic education initiated at the primary level and prepare students for tertiary education or direct entry into the labor market.

This category includes formal education programs provided within the secondary school system, generally corresponding to the International Standard Classification of Education (ISCED) levels 2 and 3. These encompass the instruction delivered in lower secondary education (15420) and upper secondary education (15420), as classified under COFOG classes 09.2.1 and 09.2.2. In the context of individual consumption, this class aligns with COICOP classes 10.2.0 (Secondary education) and 14.4.2 (Education at secondary level).

This category does not include primary education, which is classified separately, nor does it include tertiary education or non-formal vocational training programs that fall outside the scope of the secondary education system.
The same function is covered under COFOG classes 09.2.1 and 09.2.2.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 10.2.0 and 14.4.2.

This category encompasses educational programs that bridge the gap between secondary education and tertiary (higher) education. These programs typically straddle the boundaries between upper secondary and post-secondary education, focusing on specialized training or preparation that does not lead to a formal tertiary degree.

This category includes non-tertiary programs designed to provide learners with the skills and knowledge required for employment or for entry into tertiary education institutions (Post-secondary non-tertiary education). The scope corresponds to the functional requirements defined under COFOG class 09.3.0 and aligns with COICOP classes 10.3.0 and 14.4.3.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 09.3.0.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 10.3.0 and 14.4.3.

This category encompasses expenditure related to tertiary education, which covers post-secondary programmes leading to recognized academic or professional qualifications. It corresponds to the functional classification of expenditure for tertiary education as defined in the Classification of the Functions of Government (COFOG) and the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP).

This class includes all activities related to higher education, specifically those categorized under COFOG classes 09.4.1 (Tertiary education) and 09.4.2 (Tertiary education), as well as COICOP classes 10.4.0 (Tertiary education) and 14.4.4 (Tertiary education). These functions capture the provision, support, and administration of advanced educational services at the post-secondary level (15440).

This does not include educational programmes that fall outside the definitions of tertiary or higher education as specified in the referenced COFOG and COICOP classifications.
The same function is covered under COFOG classes 09.4.1 and 09.4.2.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 10.4.0 and 14.4.4.

This category encompasses educational programs and services that cannot be classified by a specific level of schooling (such as primary, secondary, or tertiary education). It focuses on specialized or supplementary educational activities that do not fit into the standard hierarchical progression of formal education systems.

This category includes educational services that are not defined by level, covering programs often categorized under administrative or supplementary educational functions. As indicated by international statistical standards, this function is equivalent to COFOG class 09.5.0 and corresponds to COICOP classes 10.5.0 (Education not definable by level) and 14.4.5.

This category does not include formal education programs that can be classified into specific levels (primary, secondary, or tertiary education), which are covered under other respective classifications of education.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 09.5.0.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 10.5.0 and 14.4.5.

This category encompasses ancillary services that facilitate and support the delivery of educational activities and the general functioning of the education system. It corresponds directly to the functional classification provided under COFOG class 09.6.0, covering services that are subsidiary to the primary provision of education.
The same function is covered under COFOG class 09.6.0.

This category encompasses government expenditure and individual consumption related to social protection services designed to support individuals and households against the risks of social exclusion, poverty, and vulnerability. It covers a broad range of social security interventions and welfare services aimed at maintaining the standard of living of the population.

This category includes social protection services as defined under the Classification of the Functions of Government (COFOG) classes 10.1.1 through 10.5.0 and 10.7.0, as well as individual consumption expenditures on social protection services as classified under the Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) classes 13.3.0 and 14.5.0 (Social protection (S)). This includes, among others, the provision of sickness and disability benefits, old-age pensions, family and child support, unemployment assistance, and housing allowances.

This category does not include social protection activities classified under COFOG 10.6.0 (Research and development social protection).

This category encompasses government expenditure and individual consumption related to social protection services, which are designed to support individuals and households against the risks of social exclusion, poverty, and vulnerability. It covers a broad range of social security interventions and welfare services aimed at maintaining the standard of living of the population.

This category includes social protection services as defined under the Classification of the Functions of Government (COFOG) classes 10.1.1 through 10.5.0 and 10.7.0. Furthermore, it corresponds to individual consumption expenditures on social protection services as classified under the Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) classes 13.3.0 (social protection services) and 14.5.0 (individual social protection services). This includes, among others, the provision of sickness and disability benefits, old-age pensions, family and child support, unemployment assistance, and housing allowances (15500).

This category does not include social protection activities classified under COFOG 10.6.0 (Research and development social protection).
The same function is covered under COFOG classes 10.1.1 to 10.5.0 and 10.7.0.  This subclass corresponds to COICOP classes 13.3.0 and 14.5.0.
